body_verbatim:
## Measured

`readTrace` (`src/engine.zig`) reads the whole trace file with no cap — after PR #322 it passes an explicit `maxInt(usize)` to the now-capped `readWhole`, with a comment saying why: every failure of that read collapses into an empty `TraceInfo`, which the caller reports as `no_shim_marker` ("the shim never initialised"). A cap added naively would relabel an oversized trace as a shim that never ran — a refusal with the wrong reason, worse than none.

The trace's size is target-controlled (it grows with the operation count), so the unbounded read is real; #265's text called the snapshot path "the one unbounded read in the engine", and this measurement says there were two.

## Proposal

Cap the trace read with its own honest outcome — `trace_truncated` already exists and is closer to the truth than `no_shim_marker`, but "truncated by the reader" and "truncated by the writer" are different facts and the report should not conflate them. Needs a small plumbing change so the cap failure is distinguishable from an unreadable file before any refusal is worded.

issue.title: readTrace is the other uncapped read, and capping it naively would relabel the failure as no_shim_marker

note: Both counts are recorded because a phrase that wraps across a line break is invisible to a line-oriented search — a mistake made twice during this sweep, in both directions. The change this issue's resolution caused is sc-03 in surface-changes.tsv.
purpose: Committed evidence for the negative claim ADR 0028 rests on: #324's body names neither the report schema's closed set nor any of its members, while the resolution attributed to it added trace_too_large to that set. The claim is a statement about an issue body, and the sweep's raw capture deliberately excludes bodies, so without this file the counterexample could not be checked by a reader (review P1-9).
